name: Krea-2 Turbo (Text-to-Image)
description: Krea-2-Turbo: a 12B Qwen-Image diffusion transformer for fast, high-quality text-to-image (8-step turbo, CFG-free). Runs the OFFICIAL krea-ai/krea-2 inference code (no ComfyUI); krea2_gguf.py overrides only the weight-loading so it can load a Q4_K_M GGUF (dequantized at load -- ~8 GB download vs 24 GB, same quality). OAIY wraps it in krea2_server.py: loads the model once, exposes POST /generate {prompt, width, height, steps, seed} -> {imageUrl}. One-click install creates a CUDA-12.8 PyTorch venv (RTX 50-series/Blackwell), clones the repo, downloads the Q4_K_M GGUF (set OAIY_KREA2_QUANT=bf16 for the full 24 GB checkpoint, or Q5_K_M/Q6_K/Q8_0) and pre-caches the Qwen3-VL-4B text encoder + Qwen-Image VAE. The transformer loads on OAIY_KREA2_DIT_DEVICE (default cuda:0); the encoder on OAIY_KREA2_ENC_DEVICE (a 2nd GPU when present, else CPU) so it fits a single 32 GB card.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# install-krea2.sh
#
# Linux setup for the "Krea-2 Turbo" text-to-image service using the OFFICIAL
# Krea-2 inference code (github.com/krea-ai/krea-2) -- no ComfyUI. Creates a
# CUDA venv, clones the repo, installs deps, downloads the Turbo checkpoint
# (~24 GB bf16), and pre-caches the Qwen3-VL-4B encoder + Qwen-Image VAE.
# Env: OAIY_BIN_DIR (= <dataDir>/bin), OAIY_HF_TOKEN (optional).

set -e

if [ -z "$OAIY_BIN_DIR" ]; then
  echo "[install-krea2] OAIY_BIN_DIR not set; run via the OAIY app/server." >&2
  exit 1
fi

dataDir=$(dirname "$OAIY_BIN_DIR")
svcDir="$dataDir/services/krea2"
repo="$svcDir/krea-2"
venv="$dataDir/venvs/krea2"
venvPy="$venv/bin/python"
# The checkpoint lives under the central models dir (any drive); the shared Qwen encoder/VAE
# stay in the default HF cache (moving them per-service forces a slow, flaky re-download).
modelsDir="${OAIY_MODELS_DIR:-$dataDir/models}"
krea2Models="$modelsDir/krea2"
ckptDir="$krea2Models/checkpoints"
fetchZip="$dataDir/scripts/fetch_zip.py"
# Validated krea-ai/krea-2 commit -- pin so an upstream model-layout change can't
# silently break the GGUF tensor-name mapping (krea2_gguf.py also asserts a match).
krea2Commit="cf3c9102c924168699b90d97a2cb15059d761488"
mkdir -p "$svcDir" "$ckptDir"

# 1. Base Python.
companionPy="$dataDir/python/bin/python3"
if [ -x "$companionPy" ]; then basePy="$companionPy"
elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then basePy="$(command -v python3)"
else echo "[install-krea2] no Python found. Run 'oaiy python install' or install python3." >&2; exit 1
fi

# 2. venv
[ -x "$venvPy" ] || { echo "[install-krea2] creating venv at $venv"; "$basePy" -m venv "$venv"; }

have_git=0
command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && have_git=1

# 3. Clone the official krea-2 repo, pinned to the validated commit. Clear any
# leftover partial dir first (an interrupted clone/extract would wedge re-runs).
if [ ! -f "$repo/inference.py" ]; then
  [ -d "$repo" ] && rm -rf "$repo"
  if [ "$have_git" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[install-krea2] fetching krea-ai/krea-2 @ $krea2Commit"
    git init -q "$repo"
    git -C "$repo" remote add origin https://github.com/krea-ai/krea-2
    if git -C "$repo" fetch --depth 1 -q origin "$krea2Commit" 2>/dev/null \
       && git -C "$repo" checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD 2>/dev/null; then :
    else
      echo "[install-krea2] warning: could not fetch pinned $krea2Commit; cloning latest (loader verifies GGUF key match)" >&2
      rm -rf "$repo"; git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/krea-ai/krea-2 "$repo"
    fi
  else
    echo "[install-krea2] git not found -- fetching krea-2 zip @ $krea2Commit"
    "$venvPy" "$fetchZip" "https://github.com/krea-ai/krea-2/archive/$krea2Commit.zip" "$svcDir"
    if [ -d "$svcDir/krea-2-$krea2Commit" ]; then mv "$svcDir/krea-2-$krea2Commit" "$repo"; else echo "[install-krea2] krea-2 zip did not contain krea-2-$krea2Commit" >&2; exit 3; fi
  fi
fi
[ -f "$repo/inference.py" ] || { echo "[install-krea2] krea-2 fetch failed" >&2; exit 3; }

# 4. PyTorch cu128 + repo deps + server deps.
echo "[install-krea2] upgrading pip"
"$venvPy" -m pip install --upgrade pip
echo "[install-krea2] installing PyTorch cu128 (large, one-time)"
"$venvPy" -m pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
echo "[install-krea2] installing krea-2 + server dependencies"
"$venvPy" -m pip install 'transformers==4.57.1' 'diffusers>=0.32.0' safetensors pillow einops click accelerate gguf 'huggingface_hub[hf_transfer,hf_xet]' fastapi 'uvicorn[standard]' requests

# 5. Download the Turbo checkpoint + pre-cache the encoder/VAE.
export HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=1
export KREA2_CKPT_DIR="$ckptDir"
# Default to the Q4_K_M GGUF (~8 GB, dequantized at load). OAIY_KREA2_QUANT=bf16
# gets the full 24 GB checkpoint; any other GGUF tag (Q5_K_M, Q6_K, ...) works too.
quant="${OAIY_KREA2_QUANT:-Q4_K_M}"
export KREA2_QUANT="$quant"
if [ "$quant" = "bf16" ]; then
  echo "[install-krea2] downloading turbo.safetensors (bf16, ~24 GB) -- this takes a while"
  "$venvPy" -c "import os; from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download; hf_hub_download('krea/Krea-2-Turbo','turbo.safetensors', local_dir=os.environ['KREA2_CKPT_DIR'], token=os.environ.get('OAIY_HF_TOKEN') or None)"
else
  echo "[install-krea2] downloading krea2_turbo-$quant.gguf (~8 GB)"
  "$venvPy" -c "import os; from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download; hf_hub_download('vantagewithai/Krea-2-Turbo-GGUF', 'krea2_turbo-' + os.environ['KREA2_QUANT'] + '.gguf', local_dir=os.environ['KREA2_CKPT_DIR'], token=os.environ.get('OAIY_HF_TOKEN') or None)"
fi

# Keep exactly one checkpoint so the server never has to choose between a GGUF and
# a bf16 leftover (also reclaims the other variant's disk).
if [ "$quant" = "bf16" ]; then keep="turbo.safetensors"; else keep="krea2_turbo-$quant.gguf"; fi
for f in "$ckptDir"/*.gguf "$ckptDir"/*.safetensors; do
  if [ -f "$f" ] && [ "$(basename "$f")" != "$keep" ]; then rm -f "$f"; fi
done

echo "[install-krea2] pre-caching Qwen3-VL-4B encoder + Qwen-Image VAE"
"$venvPy" -c "import os; from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download; tok=os.environ.get('OAIY_HF_TOKEN') or None; snapshot_download('Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct', token=tok); snapshot_download('Qwen/Qwen-Image', allow_patterns=['vae/*'], token=tok)" \
  || echo "[install-krea2] (could not pre-cache encoder/VAE; they will download on first start)"

echo "[install-krea2] done. Start the 'Krea-2 Turbo' service, then POST /generate {prompt}."

"""krea2_gguf.py -- load a Krea-2-Turbo GGUF (e.g. Q4_K_M) into the OFFICIAL
SingleStreamDiT (github.com/krea-ai/krea-2). The GGUF's tensor names match the
model's state_dict keys 1:1, so we dequantize each tensor and load it by name --
the official model + sampler code is untouched; only inference.py's
load_file()+load_state_dict() step is overridden by krea2_server.py.

Two load paths share the same dequant math:

* load_gguf_state_dict (dequant-to-bf16): the ~8 GB GGUF is dequantized once at
  load, then runs at full speed (identical math to ComfyUI's GGUF path, which
  dequantizes per-op). The win is download/disk (~8 GB vs the 24 GB bf16
  checkpoint); the dequantized weights still occupy ~24 GB of VRAM, so point
  OAIY_KREA2_DIT_DEVICE at a card with room.

* load_gguf_lowvram (on-the-fly dequant): the quantized weights stay resident
  (~8 GB) as GGUFLinear modules that dequantize per-forward. Costs a little
  compute per step but fits the DiT in ~8 GB of VRAM. The torch dequant kernels
  below are a pure-torch port of gguf.quants (verified bit-identical to the numpy
  reference) so they run on the GPU with no numpy round-trip.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


def _assert_gguf_matches_model(model, by_name: dict, gguf_path: str) -> None:
    """Fail fast + clearly if the GGUF's tensor names don't cover the model's
    state_dict -- almost always an upstream/GGUF version skew. The 1:1 name
    mapping is the load-bearing assumption of this whole loader; the installer
    pins a validated krea-ai/krea-2 commit, and a drift would otherwise corrupt
    the load silently, so we check it explicitly."""
    model_keys = set(model.state_dict().keys())
    missing = sorted(model_keys - set(by_name))
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"GGUF/model key mismatch loading {gguf_path}: {len(missing)} of "
            f"{len(model_keys)} model tensors are absent from the GGUF "
            f"(e.g. {missing[:5]}). This usually means the krea-ai/krea-2 model "
            "code drifted from the GGUF -- the installer pins a validated commit "
            "(cf3c910); re-pin the repo or use a matching GGUF/quant."
        )


def load_gguf_state_dict(model, gguf_path: str, device="cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16) -> dict:
    """Build a load-ready state_dict for `model` (an un-loaded SingleStreamDiT
    on the meta device) from the tensors in `gguf_path`."""
    from gguf import GGUFReader
    from gguf.quants import dequantize

    reader = GGUFReader(gguf_path)
    by_name = {t.name: t for t in reader.tensors}
    _assert_gguf_matches_model(model, by_name, gguf_path)

    new_sd: dict = {}
    for key, ref in model.state_dict().items():
        t = by_name[key]  # guaranteed present by _assert_gguf_matches_model
        # dequantize -> fp32 numpy in the original row-major layout; GGUF records
        # dims reversed, so reshape to the model's (out, in) shape, then cast/move.
        arr = dequantize(t.data, t.tensor_type)
        # .copy() -> a writable, owned array: dequantize returns a read-only view
        # for F16/F32 tensors, which torch.from_numpy warns about. Matches the
        # low-VRAM path; the copy is per-tensor and freed once it's on-device.
        new_sd[key] = torch.from_numpy(arr.copy()).reshape(tuple(ref.shape)).to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
    return new_sd


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# On-the-fly (low-VRAM) GGUF dequant
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Pure-torch ports of gguf.quants dequantize_blocks, vectorized over blocks (no
# python per-element loops, no numpy). Each takes a (n_blocks, type_size) uint8
# tensor and returns a (n_blocks, block_size) float32 tensor on the same device.
# The block layouts are ported 1:1 from gguf/quants.py; verified bit-identical to
# gguf.quants.dequantize for Q4_K/Q5_K/Q6_K/Q4_0/Q5_0/Q8_0.

# ggml type ids (gguf.GGMLQuantizationType)
_F32, _F16, _BF16 = 0, 1, 30
_Q4_0, _Q5_0, _Q8_0 = 2, 6, 8
_Q4_K, _Q5_K, _Q6_K = 12, 13, 14

# (block_size, type_size) per supported type -- from gguf GGML_QUANT_SIZES
_QUANT_SIZES: dict[int, tuple[int, int]] = {
    _Q4_0: (32, 18),
    _Q5_0: (32, 22),
    _Q8_0: (32, 34),
    _Q4_K: (256, 144),
    _Q5_K: (256, 176),
    _Q6_K: (256, 210),
}

_QK_K = 256


def _u8_to_f16(b: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """b: (..., 2) uint8 little-endian half -> (...) float32."""
    u16 = b[..., 0].to(torch.int32) | (b[..., 1].to(torch.int32) << 8)
    return (u16 & 0xFFFF).to(torch.int16).view(torch.float16).to(torch.float32)


def _shift(values: list[int], device, dtype=torch.uint8) -> torch.Tensor:
    return torch.tensor(values, dtype=dtype, device=device)


def _q4_k_scale_min(scales: torch.Tensor):
    """scales: (n, 12) uint8 -> (sc (n,8), min (n,8)) uint8. Ported from Q4_K.get_scale_min."""
    n = scales.shape[0]
    s = scales.reshape(n, 3, 4)
    d, m, m_d = s[:, 0, :], s[:, 1, :], s[:, 2, :]               # each (n, 4)
    sc = torch.cat([d & 0x3F, (m_d & 0x0F) | ((d >> 2) & 0x30)], dim=-1)   # (n, 8)
    mn = torch.cat([m & 0x3F, (m_d >> 4) | ((m >> 2) & 0x30)], dim=-1)     # (n, 8)
    return sc, mn


def _dequant_q4_k(blocks: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    n = blocks.shape[0]
    dev = blocks.device
    d = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, 0:2])
    dmin = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, 2:4])
    sc, m = _q4_k_scale_min(blocks[:, 4:16])
    qs = blocks[:, 16:144]
    d_s = (d.unsqueeze(1) * sc.to(torch.float32)).reshape(n, -1, 1)
    dm = (dmin.unsqueeze(1) * m.to(torch.float32)).reshape(n, -1, 1)
    q = qs.reshape(n, -1, 1, 32) >> _shift([0, 4], dev).reshape(1, 1, 2, 1)
    q = (q & 0x0F).reshape(n, -1, 32).to(torch.float32)
    return (d_s * q - dm).reshape(n, _QK_K)


def _dequant_q5_k(blocks: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    n = blocks.shape[0]
    dev = blocks.device
    d = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, 0:2])
    dmin = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, 2:4])
    sc, m = _q4_k_scale_min(blocks[:, 4:16])
    qh = blocks[:, 16:16 + _QK_K // 8]                  # (n, 32)
    qs = blocks[:, 16 + _QK_K // 8:]                    # (n, 128)
    d_s = (d.unsqueeze(1) * sc.to(torch.float32)).reshape(n, -1, 1)
    dm = (dmin.unsqueeze(1) * m.to(torch.float32)).reshape(n, -1, 1)
    ql = qs.reshape(n, -1, 1, 32) >> _shift([0, 4], dev).reshape(1, 1, 2, 1)
    qh_ = qh.reshape(n, -1, 1, 32) >> torch.arange(8, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev).reshape(1, 1, 8, 1)
    ql = (ql & 0x0F).reshape(n, -1, 32)
    qh_ = (qh_ & 0x01).reshape(n, -1, 32)
    q = (ql | (qh_ << 4)).to(torch.float32)
    return (d_s * q - dm).reshape(n, _QK_K)


def _dequant_q6_k(blocks: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    n = blocks.shape[0]
    dev = blocks.device
    ql = blocks[:, 0:_QK_K // 2]                         # (n, 128)
    qh = blocks[:, _QK_K // 2:_QK_K // 2 + _QK_K // 4]   # (n, 64)
    scales = blocks[:, _QK_K // 2 + _QK_K // 4:_QK_K // 2 + _QK_K // 4 + _QK_K // 16]  # (n, 16)
    d = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, -2:])                       # (n,)
    scales = scales.view(torch.int8).to(torch.float32)   # signed int8 scales
    d_s = (d.unsqueeze(1) * scales).reshape(n, _QK_K // 16, 1)
    ql = ql.reshape(n, -1, 1, 64) >> _shift([0, 4], dev).reshape(1, 1, 2, 1)
    ql = (ql & 0x0F).reshape(n, -1, 32)
    qh_ = qh.reshape(n, -1, 1, 32) >> _shift([0, 2, 4, 6], dev).reshape(1, 1, 4, 1)
    qh_ = (qh_ & 0x03).reshape(n, -1, 32)
    q = ((ql | (qh_ << 4)).to(torch.int8) - 32)
    q = q.reshape(n, _QK_K // 16, -1).to(torch.float32)
    return (d_s * q).reshape(n, _QK_K)


def _dequant_q4_0(blocks: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    n = blocks.shape[0]
    dev = blocks.device
    d = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, 0:2])
    qs = blocks[:, 2:18]                                 # (n, 16)
    q = qs.reshape(n, -1, 1, 16) >> _shift([0, 4], dev).reshape(1, 1, 2, 1)
    q = (q & 0x0F).reshape(n, -1).to(torch.int8) - 8     # (n, 32) in [-8, 7]
    return d.unsqueeze(1) * q.to(torch.float32)


def _dequant_q5_0(blocks: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    n = blocks.shape[0]
    dev = blocks.device
    d = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, 0:2])
    qh = blocks[:, 2:6]                                  # (n, 4) -> uint32 (5th bits)
    qs = blocks[:, 6:22]                                 # (n, 16)
    qh32 = (qh[:, 0].to(torch.int64) | (qh[:, 1].to(torch.int64) << 8)
            | (qh[:, 2].to(torch.int64) << 16) | (qh[:, 3].to(torch.int64) << 24))
    qh_bits = (qh32.reshape(n, 1) >> torch.arange(32, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev).reshape(1, 32)) & 0x01
    ql = qs.reshape(n, -1, 1, 16) >> _shift([0, 4], dev).reshape(1, 1, 2, 1)
    ql = (ql & 0x0F).reshape(n, -1).to(torch.int64)      # (n, 32)
    q = (ql | (qh_bits << 4)) - 16                       # in [-16, 15]
    return d.unsqueeze(1) * q.to(torch.float32)


def _dequant_q8_0(blocks: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    d = _u8_to_f16(blocks[:, 0:2])
    qs = blocks[:, 2:34].view(torch.int8).to(torch.float32)   # (n, 32)
    return d.unsqueeze(1) * qs


_DEQUANT_FNS = {
    _Q4_K: _dequant_q4_k, _Q5_K: _dequant_q5_k, _Q6_K: _dequant_q6_k,
    _Q4_0: _dequant_q4_0, _Q5_0: _dequant_q5_0, _Q8_0: _dequant_q8_0,
}


def dequantize_torch(raw: torch.Tensor, ggml_type: int, out_features: int,
                     in_features: int, dtype: torch.dtype = torch.bfloat16) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Dequantize a GGUF tensor's raw bytes to a (out_features, in_features) tensor.

    raw         -- uint8 tensor of the tensor's raw block bytes (any contiguous shape).
    ggml_type   -- the int gguf type id (gguf.GGMLQuantizationType value).
    Runs entirely on raw.device with pure torch ops. Bit-identical to
    gguf.quants.dequantize for the supported quant types.
    """
    if ggml_type in (_F32, _F16, _BF16):
        view_dtype = {_F32: torch.float32, _F16: torch.float16, _BF16: torch.bfloat16}[ggml_type]
        w = raw.contiguous().view(view_dtype).reshape(out_features, in_features)
        return w.to(dtype)

    fn = _DEQUANT_FNS.get(ggml_type)
    if fn is None:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"torch GGUF dequant not implemented for ggml type {ggml_type}")

    _block_size, type_size = _QUANT_SIZES[ggml_type]
    flat = raw.contiguous().reshape(-1)
    n_blocks = flat.numel() // type_size
    blocks = flat.reshape(n_blocks, type_size)
    out = fn(blocks)                                    # (n_blocks, block_size) float32
    return out.reshape(out_features, in_features).to(dtype)


class GGUFLinear(nn.Module):
    """A drop-in nn.Linear that keeps its weight quantized (GGUF bytes) and
    dequantizes on the fly each forward, so only the ~quantized weight stays
    resident in VRAM. Bias (if any) is stored dense."""

    def __init__(self, qweight: torch.Tensor, ggml_type: int, out_features: int,
                 in_features: int, bias: torch.Tensor | None = None):
        super().__init__()
        self.ggml_type = int(ggml_type)
        self.out_features = int(out_features)
        self.in_features = int(in_features)
        # raw quantized bytes (uint8); not a learnable parameter
        self.register_buffer("qweight", qweight, persistent=True)
        if bias is not None:
            self.register_buffer("bias", bias, persistent=True)
        else:
            self.bias = None

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        w = dequantize_torch(
            self.qweight, self.ggml_type, self.out_features, self.in_features, dtype=x.dtype
        )
        bias = self.bias
        if bias is not None and bias.dtype != x.dtype:
            bias = bias.to(x.dtype)
        return F.linear(x, w, bias)

    def extra_repr(self) -> str:
        return (f"in_features={self.in_features}, out_features={self.out_features}, "
                f"bias={self.bias is not None}, ggml_type={self.ggml_type}")


def _set_submodule(model: nn.Module, qualified_name: str, new_module: nn.Module) -> None:
    """setattr new_module onto its parent (model.get_submodule(parent)).<leaf>."""
    parent_name, _, leaf = qualified_name.rpartition(".")
    parent = model.get_submodule(parent_name) if parent_name else model
    if leaf.isdigit():           # ModuleList / Sequential entry
        parent[int(leaf)] = new_module
    else:
        setattr(parent, leaf, new_module)


def load_gguf_lowvram(model, gguf_path: str, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
    """Populate `model` (an un-loaded SingleStreamDiT on the meta device) from
    `gguf_path` in low-VRAM mode: every nn.Linear backed by a GGUF tensor becomes
    a GGUFLinear holding the raw quantized bytes (dequantized per-forward), while
    every other weight (RMSNorm scales, raw Parameters, biases, the F16
    `first.weight`) is dequantized once and loaded densely.

    Resident VRAM is ~the GGUF size (quantized) rather than the ~24 GB bf16 size.
    Returns the model in eval()/requires_grad_(False) with no meta tensors left.
    """
    from gguf import GGUFReader
    from gguf.quants import dequantize as np_dequantize

    reader = GGUFReader(gguf_path)
    by_name = {t.name: t for t in reader.tensors}

    # 1) Replace each nn.Linear whose weight is a GGUF tensor with a GGUFLinear
    #    holding the raw quantized bytes (+ bias) on `device`.
    handled: set[str] = set()
    linear_qnames = [name for name, mod in model.named_modules() if isinstance(mod, nn.Linear)]
    for name in linear_qnames:
        wkey = name + ".weight"
        t = by_name.get(wkey)
        if t is None:
            continue  # leave it; loaded via the dense path below (shouldn't happen for this model)
        raw = torch.from_numpy(t.data.copy()).to(device)          # uint8 block bytes
        out_features, in_features = _linear_shape(model.get_submodule(name))
        bias = None
        bkey = name + ".bias"
        bt = by_name.get(bkey)
        if bt is not None:
            barr = np_dequantize(bt.data, bt.tensor_type)
            bias = torch.from_numpy(barr.copy()).reshape(-1).to(device=device, dtype=dtype)
            handled.add(bkey)
        new = GGUFLinear(raw, int(t.tensor_type), out_features, in_features, bias=bias)
        _set_submodule(model, name, new)
        handled.add(wkey)

    # 2) Load every remaining state_dict entry densely (dequantized once).
    #    Use the post-replacement state_dict so GGUFLinear buffers are excluded.
    remaining = {k: ref for k, ref in model.state_dict().items() if k not in handled}
    dense_sd: dict = {}
    missing: list[str] = []
    for key, ref in remaining.items():
        # skip GGUFLinear's own buffers (qweight / bias) which are already set
        if key.endswith(".qweight"):
            continue
        t = by_name.get(key)
        if t is None:
            missing.append(key)
            continue
        arr = np_dequantize(t.data, t.tensor_type)
        dense_sd[key] = torch.from_numpy(arr.copy()).reshape(tuple(ref.shape)).to(device=device, dtype=dtype)

    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"GGUF {gguf_path} is missing {len(missing)} expected tensors, e.g. {missing[:5]}"
        )

    # assign_=True swaps the meta tensors for real ones (no in-place meta copy).
    model.load_state_dict(dense_sd, strict=False, assign=True)

    # Any leftover meta tensors would mean a key we never populated -- fail loudly.
    leftover = [n for n, p in model.named_parameters() if p.is_meta]
    leftover += [n for n, b in model.named_buffers() if b.is_meta]
    if leftover:
        raise RuntimeError(f"meta tensors remain after low-VRAM load, e.g. {leftover[:5]}")

    return model.eval().requires_grad_(False)


def _linear_shape(linear: nn.Linear) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """(out_features, in_features) for an nn.Linear, even on the meta device."""
    return int(linear.out_features), int(linear.in_features)
files.krea2_server.py:
"""krea2_server.py -- JSON text-to-image API over the OFFICIAL Krea-2 (K2)
inference code (github.com/krea-ai/krea-2), running the Turbo checkpoint.
No ComfyUI, no diffusers pipeline -- it imports the repo's own model code.

  GET  /health          -> {ok, loaded, model, error}
  POST /generate        -> {ok, imageUrl, imagePath, seed, model}
  GET  /file?path=<abs> -> the generated PNG bytes (guarded to the output dir)
  GET  /                 -> small JSON index

It adds the krea-2 repo dir (OAIY_KREA2_DIR) to sys.path, reuses its
_pipeline()/sample() building blocks, loads the model ONCE in a background
thread (so /health is up immediately; /generate 503s until ready), and saves
each result to disk -- returning an imageUrl pointing back at this server's
/file, the same convention as lance_server.py.

The 12B MMDiT transformer (bf16, ~24 GB) loads on OAIY_KREA2_DIT_DEVICE; the
Qwen3-VL-4B text encoder on OAIY_KREA2_ENC_DEVICE (a 2nd GPU when present, else
CPU) so it fits a single 32 GB card. OSS_TURBO may point at the checkpoint;
otherwise the checkpoints dir is scanned.

Run by the OAIY Desktop's "Krea-2 Turbo" service (cwd = the krea-2 repo):
  python krea2_server.py --server-name 127.0.0.1 --server-port 17910
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import os
import random
import sys
import threading
import time
import traceback
import urllib.parse
import uuid
import warnings
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

# The model decorates a few small fns with @torch.compile, which needs Triton
# (absent on Windows by default). Disable Dynamo so it runs eager -- correct and
# barely slower here (the compiled fns aren't the bottleneck). Override with
# OAIY_KREA2_COMPILE=1 on a box that has Triton.
if os.environ.get("OAIY_KREA2_COMPILE") != "1":
    os.environ.setdefault("TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE", "1")

# expandable_segments cuts CUDA fragmentation on Linux but is unsupported on
# Windows, where torch only warns and ignores it. Set it where it actually
# helps; the template no longer injects it via run.env, so this is the one
# switch. (Must run before `import torch` -- the allocator reads it at init.)
if not sys.platform.startswith("win"):
    os.environ.setdefault("PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF", "expandable_segments:True")

# The pinned upstream krea-2 autoencoder reads `latents_mean`/`latents_std` off
# the VAE object directly; current diffusers deprecated that access and warns
# twice at load. We pin the repo commit, so silence just that one deprecation.
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", message=r".*latents_(mean|std).*", category=FutureWarning)

import torch
import uvicorn
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Query
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

# The krea-2 repo dir (inference.py, mmdit.py, ...). On sys.path so its modules
# import; OSS_TURBO must already be set (inference.py reads it at import time).
KREA2_DIR = os.environ.get("OAIY_KREA2_DIR") or os.getcwd()
sys.path.insert(0, KREA2_DIR)

DIT_DEVICE = os.environ.get("OAIY_KREA2_DIT_DEVICE", "cuda:0")
_default_enc = "cuda:1" if torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.device_count() > 1 else "cpu"
ENC_DEVICE = os.environ.get("OAIY_KREA2_ENC_DEVICE", _default_enc)
OUTPUT_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("OAIY_KREA2_OUTPUT") or (Path(KREA2_DIR) / "outputs")).resolve()

MODEL_NAME = "krea-2-turbo"
_state = {"loaded": False, "error": None}
_dit = None
_ae = None
_enc = None
_lock = threading.Lock()  # serialize GPU jobs


class _EncoderOnDevice:
    """Wrap the encoder so sample() (which runs on the transformer's device) gets
    conditioning tensors on DIT_DEVICE in bf16 even when the encoder lives on a
    different device/dtype (e.g. fp32 on CPU)."""

    def __init__(self, enc, out_device):
        self._enc = enc
        self._out = out_device

    def __call__(self, text):
        txt, mask = self._enc(text)
        return txt.to(self._out, dtype=torch.bfloat16), mask.to(self._out)


def _load() -> None:
    global _dit, _ae, _enc
    from inference import single_mmdit_large_wide, qwen3_vl_4b
    from autoencoder import QwenAutoencoder
    from encoder import Qwen3VLConditioner
    from mmdit import SingleStreamDiT
    from safetensors.torch import load_file

    # Resolve the checkpoint: an explicit OSS_TURBO file wins; otherwise scan the
    # checkpoints dir, picking the most recently downloaded file.
    ckpt = os.environ.get("OSS_TURBO")
    if not ckpt or not os.path.isfile(ckpt):
        # Scan the configured checkpoint dir (now under the central models dir) AND the
        # legacy service-dir location, so an install made before the models-dir move still
        # loads. Most recently downloaded wins (a re-download into the new dir takes over).
        ckpt_dirs = [os.environ.get("OAIY_KREA2_CKPT_DIR"), str(Path(KREA2_DIR).parent / "checkpoints")]
        cands = []
        for _d in ckpt_dirs:
            if _d and os.path.isdir(_d):
                cands += list(Path(_d).glob("*.gguf")) + list(Path(_d).glob("*.safetensors"))
        ckpt = str(max(cands, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime)) if cands else ckpt
    if not ckpt or not os.path.isfile(ckpt):
        raise RuntimeError(f"no Krea-2 checkpoint found (OSS_TURBO={os.environ.get('OSS_TURBO')!r})")
    print(f"[krea2_server] checkpoint: {ckpt}", flush=True)

    enc_dtype = torch.float32 if str(ENC_DEVICE) == "cpu" else torch.bfloat16
    print(f"[krea2_server] loading VAE on {DIT_DEVICE} + Qwen3-VL encoder on {ENC_DEVICE}", flush=True)
    ae = QwenAutoencoder().to(DIT_DEVICE, torch.bfloat16).eval().requires_grad_(False)
    enc = Qwen3VLConditioner(qwen3_vl_4b.model_id, qwen3_vl_4b.max_length, qwen3_vl_4b.select_layers)
    enc = enc.to(ENC_DEVICE, enc_dtype).eval().requires_grad_(False)

    with torch.device("meta"):
        dit = SingleStreamDiT(single_mmdit_large_wide)
    if str(ckpt).lower().endswith(".gguf"):
        # Override the official bf16 load with our GGUF loader -- same model code,
        # quantized weights loaded by (matching) name.
        if os.environ.get("OAIY_KREA2_GGUF_LOWVRAM") == "1":
            # On-the-fly dequant: weights stay quantized (~8 GB resident) and
            # dequantize per-forward -- a little slower, but fits a smaller card.
            from krea2_gguf import load_gguf_lowvram
            print(f"[krea2_server] loading GGUF transformer (low-VRAM, on-the-fly dequant) on {DIT_DEVICE}", flush=True)
            dit = load_gguf_lowvram(dit, ckpt, device=DIT_DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        else:
            # Dequant-to-bf16: dequantize once at load (~24 GB resident), full speed.
            from krea2_gguf import load_gguf_state_dict
            print(f"[krea2_server] loading GGUF transformer (dequant-to-bf16) on {DIT_DEVICE}", flush=True)
            sd = load_gguf_state_dict(dit, ckpt, device=DIT_DEVICE, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
            dit.load_state_dict(sd, strict=True, assign=True)
            dit = dit.eval().requires_grad_(False)
    else:
        print(f"[krea2_server] loading MMDiT transformer on {DIT_DEVICE} (~24 GB bf16)", flush=True)
        dit.load_state_dict(load_file(ckpt), strict=True, assign=True)
        dit = dit.to(DIT_DEVICE, torch.bfloat16).eval().requires_grad_(False)

    _dit, _ae, _enc = dit, ae, enc
    _state["loaded"] = True
    print("[krea2_server] model loaded; ready to generate.", flush=True)


class GenerateRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str = ""
    negative: str = ""
    width: int = 1024
    height: int = 1024
    steps: int = 8
    cfg: float = 0.0      # turbo runs CFG-disabled
    mu: float = 1.15      # turbo's fixed timestep-shift
    seed: int = -1        # -1 => random


@asynccontextmanager
async def _lifespan(_app: FastAPI):
    # On Windows the ProactorEventLoop prints a ConnectionResetError traceback
    # when a client (OAIY Desktop's /health poller) drops its connection while
    # the loop is briefly stalled during the synchronous model load: the loop
    # then calls socket.shutdown() on the already-reset peer -> WinError 10054.
    # It's benign; swallow just that one so it doesn't print on every load.
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    _prev = loop.get_exception_handler()

    def _ignore_conn_reset(loop, context):
        if isinstance(context.get("exception"), ConnectionResetError):
            return
        if _prev is not None:
            _prev(loop, context)
        else:
            loop.default_exception_handler(context)

    loop.set_exception_handler(_ignore_conn_reset)
    yield


app = FastAPI(title="Krea-2 Turbo JSON API (OAIY)", lifespan=_lifespan)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])
BASE_URL = ""


def _file_url(p) -> Optional[str]:
    return f"{BASE_URL}/file?path={urllib.parse.quote(str(p))}" if p else None


@app.get("/")
def index():
    return {"service": "krea2", "model": MODEL_NAME, "generate": "POST /generate", "health": "/health"}


@app.get("/health")
def health():
    return {"ok": True, "loaded": _state["loaded"], "model": MODEL_NAME, "error": _state["error"]}


@app.get("/file")
def get_file(path: str = Query(...)):
    p = Path(path).resolve()
    if not p.is_file():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="file not found")
    if not p.is_relative_to(OUTPUT_DIR):  # path-component containment, not a string prefix
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="path not allowed")
    return FileResponse(str(p))


@app.post("/generate")
def generate(req: GenerateRequest):
    if not _state["loaded"]:
        # The model loads in a background thread at startup; a request that lands
        # mid-load waits for it (rather than 503-ing immediately), so a flow's
        # first call succeeds instead of failing.
        deadline = time.time() + 600
        while not _state["loaded"] and _state["error"] is None and time.time() < deadline:
            time.sleep(1.0)
        if not _state["loaded"]:
            return JSONResponse(status_code=503,
                                content={"ok": False, "error": _state["error"] or "model still loading"})
    from sampling import sample

    seed = req.seed if (req.seed is not None and req.seed >= 0) else random.randint(0, 2 ** 31 - 1)
    enc = _EncoderOnDevice(_enc, DIT_DEVICE)
    try:
        with _lock:  # one GPU job at a time
            imgs = sample(
                _dit, _ae, enc, [req.prompt],
                negative_prompts=([req.negative] if req.negative.strip() else None),
                device=DIT_DEVICE, width=int(req.width), height=int(req.height),
                steps=int(req.steps), guidance=float(req.cfg), seed=int(seed), mu=float(req.mu),
            )
    except Exception:
        tb = traceback.format_exc()
        print(tb, flush=True)
        return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"ok": False, "error": tb[-1800:]})

    OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fpath = (OUTPUT_DIR / f"krea2_{seed}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}.png").resolve()
    imgs[0].save(str(fpath))
    return {"ok": True, "imageUrl": _file_url(fpath), "imagePath": str(fpath), "seed": seed, "model": MODEL_NAME}


def main() -> None:
    global BASE_URL
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Krea-2 Turbo JSON API server")
    ap.add_argument("--server-name", default="127.0.0.1")
    ap.add_argument("--server-port", type=int, default=17910)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    host = args.server_name if args.server_name not in ("0.0.0.0", "::", "") else "127.0.0.1"
    BASE_URL = f"http://{host}:{int(args.server_port)}"

    print(f"[krea2_server] starting; loading model in background (dit={DIT_DEVICE}, enc={ENC_DEVICE}).", flush=True)

    def _bg():
        try:
            _load()
        except Exception:
            _state["error"] = traceback.format_exc()
            print(_state["error"], flush=True)

    threading.Thread(target=_bg, daemon=True).start()
    uvicorn.run(app, host=args.server_name, port=int(args.server_port), log_level="info")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
